text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for service `inference-gateway` (latency > 99th pct). Incident ID PD-8472. Urgency: high. Trigger: p99 latency > 1200ms for 2 mins. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-8472

pagerduty: PD-8472 page fired. Routing policy: primary oncall sophia.

sophia: on it, grabbing laptop. will ack in PD.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: page still unacknowledged after 75s. Escalation policy step 2: paging secondary and manager.

pagerduty: Escalation: paging @jamal (secondary) and @manager-lia (manager). PD-8472 assigned to jamal.

jamal: ACKed in PD. standing by. @sophia if you can join, otherwise i'll start triage.

sophia: omg my phone died walking to kitchen, brb 30s. thanks for the pickup.

jamal: quick status: p99 latency spike concentrated on inference-gateway nodes in eu-west-1. Error-rate not elevated, just very long tails. dashboard: https://grafana.example/d/xy9/gateway-latency

erin: saw some 502s earlier when gateway timed out talking to model-router. forwarding last 10m logs.

jamal: pulling logs from one affected pod: `kubectl logs gateway-66f9 -n prod`

jamal: ```
2026-03-14T02:11:21Z WARN connection: slow downstream ack (1.8s)
2026-03-14T02:11:22Z ERROR router: upstream request timed out after 10s to model-router-2
2026-03-14T02:11:23Z INFO retries: attempting failover to router-3
```

jamal: looks like model-router-2 is intermittently delaying requests. Not a full crash but severe degradation. Can someone check model-router pods and their JVM metrics?

erin: on it. `kubectl top pod -n prod | grep model-router` shows router-2 with 95% CPU and steep heap growth. GC logs show repeated full GCs.

manager-lia: if router node is GC-thrashing, we should fail traffic away and scale up router replicas, also notify customer-facing channels if SLOs breached.

incident-bot: Automatic mitigation: traffic split policy applied - 40% traffic moved off eu-west-1 to eu-west-2 to reduce tail.

jamal: applying quick mitigation: bump model-router replicaCount to 6 (was 3) and trigger rolling restart of router-2.```

jamal: `kubectl set resources deploy/model-router -n prod --limits=cpu=2000m` (temporary), `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-router -n prod --field-selector=metadata.name=model-router-2`

incident-bot: mitigation action executed: replicas scaled; restart requested for router-2. Monitoring for p99.

sophia: back online, acked in PD. joining. thanks.

jamal: after restart, router-2 shows lower heap and GC normalizing. p99 dropped from 1.6s to 400ms over 3 minutes. Grafana: https://grafana.example/d/xy9/gateway-latency?from=now-10m

erin: did a quick heapdump analysis: the router had a regression in a recent dependency that increased object retention during warmup; rolled back that dependency in canary yesterday but apparently hit prod via a separate deploy.

manager-lia: action items: (1) roll back offending artifact across routers, (2) add a strong JVM GC alert (sustained full GCs > 3 in 5m), (3) add p99 latency alert escalation to include manager at step 2 only if unacknowledged for >60s.

jamal: adding notes to PD ticket. current service impact: p99 elevated for ~12m, estimated affected requests ~800/min at peak, user-facing errors ~0.6%. No data loss.

sophia: notifying on-call support that CS might receive tickets; CC: support-runbook link: https://docs.internal/support/runbooks/gateway-timeouts

oncall-ops: acknowledged. we'll track customer reports and surface any P1.

incident-bot: PD-8472 acknowledged by jamal and sophia; resolved at 1851004987. Resolution note: model-router instability due to dependency regression; rolling restart and replica scale mitigated tail latency. Postmortem owner: infra-sre.

manager-lia: thanks for quick work. we'll schedule RCA and postmortem. please include timeline, deploy audit, and a proposed alerting change. closing once runbook updated. :white_check_mark:

sophia: quick personal note - will update my oncall checklist to carry a powerbank. lesson learned 😅

jamal: follow-ups tracked in PD-8472 and infra board. assigning infra-sre as owner. ETA postmortem draft: 48h.

oncall-ops: taking handoff for follow-ups. closing thread here.
